:::{#thm-mutual-information-nonnegative}
#### Mutual information is nonnegative

For [discrete random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$ and $Y$
with finite [entropies](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy),

$$\mutinfof{X}{Y} \ge 0.$$

Equality holds exactly when $X$ and $Y$ are
[independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt).

:::

::: {.proof}

Let $p(x, y)$ be the [joint mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-pmf), with [marginals](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-marginal) $p(x)$ and $p(y)$.
By @thm-mutual-information-kl,
$\mutinfof{X}{Y}$ is the divergence of $p(x) \, p(y)$ from $p(x, y)$,
and the [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation) defining it is absolutely summable,
as the proof of that result shows.
The product $p(x) \, p(y)$ is positive wherever $p(x, y)$ is positive,
because each of $p(x)$ and $p(y)$ is at least $p(x, y)$ there.
By @thm-kl-divergence-nonnegative, the divergence is nonnegative,
with equality exactly when $p(x) \, p(y)$ and $p(x, y)$ agree.
The [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) satisfies $\log_b t = \ln t / \ln b$,
so the divergence with $\log_b$
is the divergence with $\log_2$ times $\ln 2 / \ln b$,
which has the same sign and the same zero.
Hence $\mutinfof{X}{Y} \ge 0$,
and $\mutinfof{X}{Y} = 0$ exactly when $p(x, y) = p(x) \, p(y)$ for every pair,
which is independence.

:::
